title: slim versions?
description:
I've found the `-slim` variants of the official Python images to work well and we now use them in our Python images in the geocompx project: https://github.com/geocompx/docker/blob/2ba2fa7068630118de1fc624347fabf32cc57b28/python/Dockerfile#L1 

Are there any plans to offer slim variants of the bookworm-based images here? Could lead to smaller sizes and as a result better user experience and perhaps even slightly lower energy use if so.

description:

Do we have a philosophy around whether the `r-base` image should be considered a "batteries-included" image, so that the more commonly-used R packages will function, or is it intended to be more minimal?

title: add multiarch image / arm support
description:
especially for people using Apple Silicon, it might be convenient to have a multiarch image with arm support (ie. `linux/arm64` or something).

If I understand this correctly, using the existing `linux/amd64` image on Apple Silicon would involve some kind of emulation (QEMU? Rosetta? Both? I don't know ...), which may carry a (further) performance penalty.

The [official r-base](https://hub.docker.com/layers/r-base/library/r-base/4.1.2/images/sha256-fc6f3bac82f6f732114abc019bf1558b1430adb31a3ae5bdd720973879adb554?context=explore) seems to have this.

title: TinyTeX fails to install on older distros
description:
Builds for older distros like Ubuntu 16, CentOS 7, and openSUSE 42 currently fail on the TinyTeX installation: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/rstudio/r-docker/375/workflows/88494032-53f9-4406-b5d7-d48e7b71b504/jobs/2750

There's an issue for this at https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/280, so we'll just monitor that for a while.

title: The 4.0.3 image is twice as big as 4.0.2
set snapshotted RSPM binaries as default CRAN mirror
description:
expanding on #32 it might be helpful if the images shipped with the appropriate RSPM url, as in `repos = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/__linux__/bionic/279"` for Ubuntu Bionic, etc.

The rocker images have a neat practice where R releases get CRAN set to `latest` on the MRAN checkpoint server *or* to whatever latest snapshot was taken when, say, R 3.6.3 was still `release`.
This way, even the old images will, by default, "just work" and install the appropriate dependencies.

Though these kinds of black magic do of course increase the complexity.

title: Slim / alpine versions?
description:
Docker has official 'slim' runtimes for a number of programming languages, e.g. [python:slim](https://github.com/docker-library/python/blob/c3233a936f58bee7c6899d3e381f23ed12cfc7a8/3.7/buster/slim/Dockerfile) and [ruby:slim](https://github.com/docker-library/ruby/blob/master/2.6/buster/slim/Dockerfile). It might be useful to provide a similar thing for R also based on `debian:buster-slim`.

Similarly a distribution based on alpine linux might be useful to the community, as using alpine is pretty popular due to its small size.

title: Set the TZ variable
description:
R 3.4 generates a warning during `R CMD check` (it happens whenever `Sys.timezone()` is called) when run under docker

> Warning: running command 'timedatectl' had status 1

However setting the `TZ` environment variable avoids this, e.g. to `UTC`. Is there any chance we could set this automatically for the 3.4 container?

Other versions of R either do not try to call timedatectl, or fail more gracefully if it does not exist, but 3.4 will always generate this warning.

Doing it automatically here would avoid users' running into this if these containers are used in CI settings.

title: R-devel versions?
description:
It would be useful to have a daily containers built with R-devel, so that we could use them on CI systems and for local testing. Once a day would be more than enough I think. 

CRAN explicitly says that new packages must run R CMD check with R-devel before submission, so this would be something generally useful to (a subset) of customers as well.

Probably requires https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/issues/6 to be completed first.

title: Should containers set a default CRAN mirror?
description: It might be nice if the docker container set a default CRAN mirror in the site .RProfile, to either cloud.r-project.org or cran.rstudio.org. There are billed as an opinionated builds, so I don't foresee any real issues.

title: Follow Dockerfile Best Practices
description:
https://docs.docker.com/develop/develop-images/dockerfile_best-practices/#sort-multi-line-arguments

Specifically "&& rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*", but applied to other OSes and fetched files as well.

title: SLES 15 sysdep problems
description:
@glin @slopp 

Feedback on SLES 15 (using an AWS AMI, I believe? @ChaitaC may be able to provide more direction about the image she used):
When executing the sysdeps command:
```
No provider of 'pango-tools' found.
'atlascpp-devel' not found in package names. Trying capabilities.
No provider of 'atlascpp-devel' found.
'libreadline6' not found in package names. Trying capabilities.
No provider of 'libreadline6' found.
```

I then installed the following (shooting for parity, but unsure if this was required):
```
pango-devel
libreadline7
```
I could not find anything in `zypper search` that was `atlas` related

R worked (slightly), but threw errors that required installing:
```
libblas3
liblapack3
```

Then an error in running `capabilities()`:
```
Warning message:
In doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler) :
  unable to load shared object '/opt/R/3.6.0/lib/R/modules//R_X11.so':
  libjpeg.so.62: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

Resolved by:
```
zypper install -y libjpeg62
```

OS details:
```
> cat /etc/os-release
NAME="SLES"
VERSION="15"
VERSION_ID="15"
PRETTY_NAME="SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15"
ID="sles"
ID_LIKE="suse"
ANSI_COLOR="0;32"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:suse:sles:15"
```
